0|676d23690fb62b5d51ba5d659935e9f7d9da9f8e|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"net: Fix use after free by removing length arg from sk_data_ready callbacks.
Several spots in the kernel perform a sequence like:
skb_queue_tail(&sk->s_receive_queue
sk->sk_data_ready(sk
But at the moment we place the SKB onto the socket receive queue it
can be consumed and freed up.  So this skb->len access is potentially
to freed up memory.
Furthermore
column2: the skb->len can be modified by the consumer so it is

column1: possible that the value isn't accurate.
And finally
column2: no actual implementation of this callback actually uses

column1: the length argument.  And since nobody actually cared about it's
value
column2: lots of call sites pass arbitrary values in such as '0' and

column1: even '1'.
So just remove the length argument from the callback
is no confusion whatsoever and all of these use-after-free cases get
fixed as a side effect.
Based upon a patch by Eric Dumazet and his suggestion to audit this
issue tree-wide.
